A local SEO checklist for service-area businesses

Local search is where most homeowners start. A checklist of the fundamentals that help established service companies show up for the jobs they want.

Savvy Team Growth strategy · Savvy Post Marketing

Published June 24, 2026 · 5 min read

Start with your business profile

For many local searches, your business profile appears before your website. Treat it as a page in its own right.

  • Primary category matches your main service; secondary categories cover the rest.
  • Service area set to where you actually want work.
  • Hours, phone and booking link are accurate and tracked.
  • Recent photos of real jobs, crews and vehicles.
  • Services listed with short, plain descriptions.

Build pages that match real searches

Customers search for a service and a place: “water heater replacement” plus a town name. Your site should have a clear page for each core service, and well-written pages for the main areas you serve.

  • One page per core service, with pricing guidance where you can give it.
  • Area pages with genuinely local detail, not copied text with a new town name.
  • Clear calls to action: call, book online, request an estimate.
  • Fast loading on mobile.

“Write for the customer in the town, not for the search engine.”

Avoid the temptation to target every town within driving distance. A smaller set of well-built pages for the areas where you want more work, and can serve profitably, usually performs better than dozens of thin ones.

Make reviews a habit

Reviews influence both rankings and decisions. The difference between businesses with a steady stream of reviews and those without is rarely quality; it’s whether anyone asks.

  • Ask at the right moment: when the job is done and the customer is happy.
  • Make it easy with a direct link by text.
  • Reply to every review, especially the critical ones.

In practice · Cleaning

A review request sent automatically two hours after a completed clean, with the cleaner’s name in the message.

Keep the basics consistent

Consistency checklist
ItemWhere to check
Business nameProfile, website, directories, social
Address or service areaProfile, website footer, directories
Phone numberUse tracking numbers carefully so the main number stays consistent
Website linkProfile and directories point to the right page

Content that earns local trust

Beyond service pages, a small amount of genuinely useful content helps both search visibility and conversion. Think of the questions your office answers every week: how long a job takes, what it typically costs, what to do before the crew arrives. Answer them clearly on your site, and link to those answers from your profile and booking confirmations.

Project pages are particularly effective for established businesses. A short write-up of a real job in a real neighbourhood, with photos and what the customer needed, shows experience in a way a list of services cannot. It also gives you something specific to share on your profile and social channels.

Keep it maintained. An outdated page with old prices or a retired service does more harm than good, so review your core pages at least twice a year.

Measure the outcome

Rankings are a means, not the goal. Track calls, booking requests and booked jobs from local search, using the same source discipline as every other channel.

Your checklist for this quarter

  1. Audit your business profile against the list above.
  2. Identify the two services where your pages are weakest and rewrite them.
  3. Set up an automatic review request after completed jobs.
  4. Track booked jobs from local search for 90 days.

Key takeaways

  • Your business profile is often the first page customers see.
  • Service and area pages should match how customers search.
  • Reviews need a system, not occasional requests.
  • Consistency of name, address and phone still matters.
